A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedBis/FedBiscuit study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original summarization and question-answering experiments in Tables 1–2, selector-size comparisons in Appendix B.3, and generated examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and Appendix B.3, together with the generated examples in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The selector training, clustering, aggregation, majority voting, DPO, and LoRA procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 adds a secure-aggregation recommendation, without documenting its integration into the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain TL;DR summarization and SHP-based question answering, with the same Reddit/SafeRLHF prompt sources and AlpacaEval evaluation. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Appendix C retain the same Raw Model, FedAvg, and FedDPO comparators. The FedBis/FedBiscuit configurations and Appendix B.3 comparison methods also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 6–7.1 and Appendix B retain the same partitions, model configurations, training settings, checkpoint selection, and evaluation procedures, including 6,553 summarization samples and 805 QA instructions.

E4.justification: The selector and ensemble comparisons, prompt-source and completion-count analyses, Appendix B.3 model-size comparison, and Appendix C case studies are retained. No new ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same plus/minus uncertainty reporting. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 6 retain the same entries, scores, win/tie counts, and uncertainty values. For example, FedBis with the Qwen-2-0.5B selector still achieves 86.69% summarization win rate for Gemma-2B. Appendix C outputs also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, clustering constraint, aggregation equations, and DPO formulation in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A remain equivalent. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about federated preference collection, the benchmark, improved generation, and addressing preference heterogeneity and reward hacking.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly discusses the server inferring preferences from individual client models and identifies secure aggregation as a safeguard. Existing interpretations of experimental results and other limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project code-repository link beneath the abstract, providing new access information. Hardware, hyperparameters, data preparation, and prompt templates remain unchanged; repository contents and availability are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 expands citations concerning LLMs, federated tuning, resource constraints, and secure aggregation. These additions broaden supporting context without substantially changing the positioning against centralized RLHF and FedDPO.

P1.justification: v3 adds brief selector-efficiency explanations, an explicit Algorithm 1 reference, and acknowledgements, alongside localized wording and bibliography edits. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 enlarges Tables 1–2, adjusts algorithm spacing, adds conference headers, and makes minor caption edits. Pagination and surrounding text shift, but all figures and tables retain their underlying content and structure.

improvement.justification: The added code-access pointer, more readable main results tables, and brief explanatory refinements modestly improve usability and documentation. Appendix A.1 also identifies a relevant privacy safeguard, although its implementation and effectiveness are not demonstrated. The scientific methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
